messages:
emily_cust: hi — our prod app started getting 403s for /v1/infer yesterday evening. first seen ~2026-03-15T18:12:23Z. example request id from response header: 0b3f9c2e-9f2a-4d1a-bc7a-6e8a2f5e7c11. using a service key created by infra. any idea?

sara_support: sorry about that — can you paste a minimal curl you used (redact the token) and the exact response body/headers? also let us know whether this is a service account key or a user token and the org/project it should be hitting.

emily_cust: sure — here's a redacted curl and raw response we captured:```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*****REDACTED*****" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org-kr8p" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}'
```response (headers + body):```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2026 18:12:23 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: 0b3f9c2e-9f2a-4d1a-bc7a-6e8a2f5e7c11

{"error":"request_signature_mismatch","message":"token scope does not allow project invocation"}
```This is intermittent — sometimes same key works for other endpoints (embeddings) but infer fails.

ben_eng: hmm interesting. two quick guesses: 1) service key might be scoped to org-level read but not project invoke; 2) there might be a mismatch between the X-Org-Id header and the org encoded in the key (org roaming). can you confirm which key type: "service_key" (created via infra) vs "user_token"? also paste the response headers when it works (if you have them).

emily_cust: it's a terraform-created service_key assigned to infra team. tf output: "service_key_id = sk-infra-94f". we do have both an org header and the project id in the request body in our app normally. here's a case where embeddings succeeded right before the infer 403 — headers for the success request:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-Id: d4f7a8b2-2c3e-4f25-8a3a-1a9c5b0f1122
Content-Type: application/json
```but infer returns 403 with the 0b3f9c... id.

marco_se: can you try reproducing with two quick variants locally: 1) swap the token for a project-scoped token and 2) remove the X-Org-Id header (to see if our routing is picking org from header vs token). josh_repro has a small repro script that automates both — @josh_repro can you drop it here?

josh_repro: pasted a tiny repro script — run like `./repro.sh <token> <org-id>`.```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
TOKEN=$1
ORG=$2
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: $ORG" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"test"}'
```run both with the service key and with a project-scoped token and paste headers.

emily_cust: ran both. results: service key -> 403 (same body), project token -> 200. so looks scoped. commands I ran:```bash
./repro.sh sk-infra-***** org-kr8p  # -> 403, X-Request-Id: 0b3f9c2e-9f2a...
./repro.sh pt-prod-12345 org-kr8p   # -> 200, X-Request-Id: a7b1c3d4-5589-4f2a-98c1-33f9b8e2d444
```so that suggests the service_key lacks the invoke scope for the project. is there a way to verify scopes attached to sk-infra-94f?

sara_support: thanks — that pattern is helpful. can you run `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` with the service key and paste the response? that should show the token type and allowed scopes. if you prefer, share the Service Key ID and we can look it up from our side (we'll only check scopes).

emily_cust: whoami with the service key returns:```json
{"token_type":"service_key","id":"sk-infra-94f","scopes":["org:read","models:list"]}```no project:invoke scope present. how do we add it? our infra team assumed service keys get project invoke by default.

ben_eng: that's the root cause then. service keys created with infra role only get org-level scopes — embedding endpoints are allowed under org:read/models:list for your setup, but infer requires project:invoke. two options: 1) create a project-scoped token or 2) update the service key scopes (if your infra process allows). I'll flag the policy docs.

emily_cust: ok we'll switch to project token for now but curious why this started happening intermittently — why would the same service key sometimes work?

marco_se: intermittent success often comes from request routing or fallback to a different model variant that accepts org-level calls (legacy paths). can you share the working request id (the embeddings one) and the failing infer id (you already did). I'll pull traces. @ops-bot can you collect a debug bundle for both request ids?

ops-bot: debug collection started for request ids [d4f7a8b2-2c3e-4f25-8a3a-1a9c5b0f1122, 0b3f9c2e-9f2a-4d1a-bc7a-6e8a2f5e7c11]. debug bundle available: https://debug.redwood.ai/bundles/1768456789-0b3f9c2e-collection.zip (expires in 7 days). please include any server-side logs you have when you ran the repro.

emily_cust: uploaded our client logs to the bundle (link in the debug page). quick question: is there any permission change on our org that could strip service key scopes? we didn't change infra tf for that key recently.

ben_eng: scope stripping usually only happens on explicit key rotate or a policy update in the org defaults. we'll check audit logs. sara_support — can you escalate to auth-team with the service_key id and request ids and include the debug bundle link?

sara_support: filing now — auth-team pinged. summary in ticket: service_key sk-infra-94f lacks project:invoke, repro shows project token works, debug bundle + request ids attached. tagging @auth-team for policy/audit check.

marco_se: auth-team responded in ticket: policy change was rolled to org-kr8p last week tightening service key defaults (removed implicit project:invoke). they listed affected keys. auth team can retroactively add scopes to specific keys if needed or advise rotating to project tokens.

emily_cust: ok thanks — we'll provision a project token and update infra. appreciate the fast help. :thumbsup:

sara_support: glad it's narrowed down. leaving this thread open for any follow-up, but closing the immediate support escalation since it's a scope/policy config. if you want us to re-add scopes to the service key, reply here and we'll coordinate auth-team change requests.

emily_cust: follow-up: could you add a quick note in docs or an alert when creating service keys so infra folks don't assume project:invoke is included? ran into this blind spot.

ben_eng: good call — i'll add a short blurb to the service-key onboarding doc and a CLI warning when creating keys without project scopes. will follow up with a PR.

ops-bot: tagging done: issue #RFC-322 created for improving service-key UX.
